subject: Recap: Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-call) / Next steps
msg_1_body:
Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our call.

Key asks we captured: 
- Latency targets: p95 generation latency target for short responses (<=256 tokens) — Finova aiming for <=200ms p95; tail SLOs for long generations ok to be higher.
- Throughput / concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency ~200 reqs in US, ~50 in EU, ~30 in APAC during peak.
- Streaming: client needs chunked streaming; first-byte latency (time-to-first-chunk) should be prioritized (target <150ms p95).
- Regional routing & data residency: traffic should route to regionally isolated pools by customer geography. EU customer data must remain in EU-only tenancy; APAC similarly; US can use hosted region.

Proposed immediate next steps: 
1) We'll send an architecture + SLO proposal with numeric capacity estimates and routing plan (ETA: 24–48 hours).
2) Confirm whether Finova is ok with geo-failover (i.e., route to nearest region by default, with explicit account-level residency overrides).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive to validate streaming behavior and run a short perf test (30–45 minutes).

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (draft), network-arch-diagram.png (initial).

If the above looks right, please confirm the numbers or call out any changes and we'll finalize the proposal.

—Marissa

msg_2_subject: Re: Recap: Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-call)
msg_2_body:
Thanks Marissa — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: goal is p95 <=120ms for very short prompts (single-turn customer messages); an overall p95 <=200ms for general usage is acceptable, but the first-byte for streaming is most important for UX.
- Throughput: peak concurrent connections are likely to hit ~200 in the US; EU and APAC numbers are as you captured (50 / 30). We expect bursts up to 2x during marketing promos — need burst capacity.
- Streaming: chunked streaming is required. First-chunk <150ms p95, subsequent chunk cadence ~100–200ms typical.
- Data residency: EU must stay in EU (no replication to US). APAC must be isolated when requested; some accounts will require on-prem or VPC-only.

Question: for EU residency, is Redwood able to offer isolated control plane + data plane, or would we need a Private deployment?

If you can include the control-plane/residency options in the proposal that would be great — we can then route the procurement team accordingly. Happy to join the tech deep-dive next Tue or Wed.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
samir.patel@finova.com
msg_3_subject: Re: Recap: Performance SLOs & Regional Routing (post-call) — proposal attached
msg_3_body:
Hi Samir — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a short proposal and an architecture sketch addressing the control-plane / data-plane options and residency constraints. High-level summary: 

- Deployment options: 
  * Hosted (recommended for quickest time-to-value) — regional data partitioning, control plane in Redwood; data residency controls for EU via regional tenancy and encryption-at-rest with KMS.
  * Private (VPC/Private deployment) — isolated control plane and data plane, recommended for regulated accounts that require no cross-region control-plane access.

- Performance proposal (short prompts, <=256 tokens): 
  * US: dedicated pool sized for 200 steady concurrent with autoscale for 2x bursts (suggest initial reserve 4x A100-equivalent slots). p95 generation <=150–200ms achievable with model selection + lower quantization tradeoffs.
  * EU: isolated pool with 50 steady concurrency, burst to 100; same p95 targets. Must be a separate tenancy for strict residency.
  * APAC: smaller dedicated pool, 30 steady concurrency; consider single-tenant or partner-hosted region if on-prem required.

- Streaming: we will prioritize time-to-first-chunk with continuous batching disabled for first-token; subsequent tokens use adaptive batching. Expect first-chunk <150ms p95 in regional pools.

- Routing: geo-based routing by default; account-level residency override to pin to EU/APAC pools. Fallback behavior: if pinned region is unavailable, we can fail closed or fail open by policy — recommend fail closed for EU-residency accounts.

Next steps proposed: 
1) Confirm residency policy (fail closed vs fail open) per account.
2) Schedule 45-minute tech deep-dive (Aditya/Neha to lead) — propose Tue 10/27 or Wed 10/28.
3) We will include pricing and estimated monthly committed capacity in the formal proposal.

I'll loop in Aditya for technical sizing and Neha for compliance on the SOC2/KMS plan.

Best,
—Marissa
msg_4_subject: Internal: Feasibility notes — Finova multi-region SLOs
msg_4_body:
Marissa / Neha — quick notes after reviewing the numbers: 

- Latency: hitting p95 <=150–200ms for short prompts is achievable in-region if we: 
  * Use a light-weight model variant for short-turn chat (fewer decoder tokens),
  * Keep KV cache warm for active sessions,
  * Prioritize first-token by temporarily bypassing batching for new streams.

- Concurrency & throughput: 200 steady concurrent (US) requires roughly N GPU slots; initial recommendation: reserve capacity for 200 steady (4–6 mid-sized GPUs depending on model) and set autoscale to 2x for burst. We'll provide exact GPU counts in the proposal after we pick model/quantization tradeoffs.

- Data residency: EU strict residency => separate VPC/tenancy and KMS keys. We can support hosted EU with isolated data plane + customer-managed KMS, but if Finova requires isolated control-plane we should recommend Private deployment.

- Streaming behavior: ensure first-chunk <150ms — we can do this by dedicating a small pool that skips batching for initial tokens. Slight increase in cost but huge UX benefit.

Action items: Aditya to produce per-region GPU sizing + cost estimate; Neha to draft compliance/residency language and confirm whether hosted+customer-managed KMS meets Finova procurement. Recommend we attach SOC2 summary and network diagram to the next customer email.

- Aditya
